questions.q: What is an evasion attack, as distinct from the general concept of an adversarial example?
options: An attack that steals a model's weights through repeated API queries
An attack at inference time against a deployed classifier, aimed at getting a malicious or undesired input past detection
An attack that poisons a model's training data before it is ever deployed
An attack that floods an API endpoint with requests until it becomes unavailable
questions.explain: Evasion attacks target an already-deployed detection model at inference time, with the specific goal of getting a malicious input classified as benign.

questions.q: Why is evading a real malware classifier a harder problem than the panda/gibbon image example?
options: Malware classifiers are never trained on real malware samples
Antivirus vendors do not use machine learning in practice
Malware files cannot be represented as numeric feature vectors
The perturbed file still has to execute and carry its payload — most arbitrary byte-level changes would corrupt or break its functionality
questions.explain: Unlike pixel noise on an image, a modification to a malware binary must preserve the file's ability to actually run and do what it was built to do, which sharply constrains what an attacker can change.

questions.q: What is the real difference between a feature-space attack and a problem-space attack?
options: A feature-space attack perturbs the numeric vector a model sees; a problem-space attack must perturb the real artifact itself while keeping it realizable and functional
A feature-space attack only works against text classifiers, while a problem-space attack only works against image classifiers
A problem-space attack is always easier to execute than a feature-space attack
There is no practical difference between the two once a perturbation is computed mathematically
questions.explain: Feature-space perturbations are convenient mathematically but don't necessarily map back to a real, working artifact; problem-space attacks must survive translation into an actual file, email, or packet.

questions.q: What does 'functionality-preserving' mean when researchers describe an evasion technique against a malware classifier?
options: A perturbation that deletes the malware's payload entirely so it cannot be analyzed
A perturbation applied only after a human has manually reviewed and approved the sample
A real, problem-space modification to a malicious file — such as padding bytes or unused code sections — that evades detection while the file still performs its intended malicious function
A perturbation that only exists inside a classifier's training set, never in a deployed file
questions.explain: Functionality-preserving is the key constraint in real-world evasion research: the file must still behave as malware after the modification, not just fool the classifier in theory.

questions.q: What is a 'good word attack' against a spam or phishing filter?
options: Replacing a phishing email's malicious link with a benign one
Training a spam filter on a larger, cleaner dataset
Encrypting the entire body of a phishing email so the filter cannot parse it
Inserting or substituting words and characters associated with legitimate mail to dilute a filter's detection signal, without destroying the message's ability to phish its target
questions.explain: Good word attacks exploit which words and characters a filter's training data associates with legitimate mail, diluting the detection signal while the message still functions as a phishing attempt.
